documents.title: Our AI Policy (Writing Center)
documents.summary: The University of Miami Writing Center states how its consultants handle AI: they follow each instructor's and publication's rules, may recommend AI tools only where allowed, and emphasize ethics, attribution and critical thinking. It is a unit-level statement, not a university-wide policy, and it discloses that ChatGPT helped draft it.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no AI rule of its own: 'our support aligns with the guidelines and expectations set by each professor for that class and the individual assignment', so the decision is handed to instructors, which makes the stance delegates.

units.why: States that AI 'can be valuable tools for writing and research', a benefit claim rather than a rule, so informs; P87 (benefits) fits because it is not tied to careers or a rule.
units.anchor: artificial intelligences (AIs) can be valuable tools for writing and research

units.why: Says writers 'will need to be able to effectively and ethically engage with these tools inside and outside of academia', a professional-readiness reason for engaging with AI, so P44.
units.anchor: writers will need to be able to effectively and ethically engage with these tools

units.why: The primary approach is that support 'aligns with the guidelines and expectations set by each professor for that class and the individual assignment', so the instructor decides; P04 fits (rule set per instructor and assignment).
units.anchor: our support aligns with the guidelines and expectations set by each professor
units.frag_start: When working with students, our primary
units.fit_note: Addressed to the Writing Center's own consulting support rather than to students, but the rule is the same: the instructor sets what AI use is allowed.

units.why: For publication work, consultants 'align our support with the professional guidelines for that publication', deferring to venue rules, which is P62 (AI in scholarship, deferring to venue rules).
units.anchor: align our support with the professional guidelines for that publication
units.frag_start: When clients are working towards publications,
units.fit_note: Covers writing consulting for publications, not formal research rules. Covers deferring to a publication's guidelines for clients' writing, not theses, grants or peer review specifically.

units.why: Instructors are asked to 'be clear about your expectations for student use of AI, ideally in writing, either in your syllabus or on your assignment sheet', an AI statement request; P09, and the soft 'please' makes it should.
units.anchor: Please be clear about your expectations for student use of AI, ideally in writing
units.fit_note: A request ('ideally in writing'), not a firm requirement, and justified so that Writing Center staff can follow it.

units.why: Students are told 'Please be aware of your instructor's AI expectations' before sessions; this is the duty to know each course's rules, P78 rather than P10 because it does not say to ask.
units.anchor: Please be aware of your instructor's AI expectations when meeting with your writing center consultant

units.why: Asks students to 'bring them to your session' if they have written instructor AI guidelines, a procedure for passing the rules to staff; nearest type P78 (students follow each course's rules).
units.anchor: AI guidelines from your instructor in writing, please bring them to your session.
units.fit_note: Adds that students hand the written rules to the consultant; P78 only covers learning and following the rules. Asks students to bring written instructor guidelines to a session so consultants can follow them; goes beyond knowing the rules.

units.why: Says staff 'can help students understand and use AI effectively and ethically', i.e. help is offered to teach effective AI use, closest to P44 but about a support service.
units.anchor: Our staff can help students understand and use AI effectively and ethically
units.frag_end: effectively and ethically, emphasizing the following:
units.fit_note: A service offered by staff rather than a professional-skill claim; fits P44's 'courses teach or demonstrate AI use'.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this. The source says 'Our staff can help students understand and use AI effectively and ethically', a statement of the service staff offer and so a real statement about teaching AI use; kept as P44 (teach effective AI use) with a fit_note because it is a service, not a professional-skill claim. Coder B did not code it.

units.why: Consultants 'will not recommend AI tools to students that violate instructors' expectations or academic integrity', a staff limit tied to the instructor's rule; P04 is the closest type since the instructor's expectations control.
units.anchor: Consultants will not recommend AI tools to students that violate instructors' expectations
units.fit_note: Also bars recommending tools that violate academic integrity; it limits staff recommendations, not student use. B coded P59 (instructor AI use), which does not fit because consultants are not instructors and this is not their own AI use.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P04, coder B coded P59. The source says 'Consultants will not recommend AI tools to students that violate instructors' expectations or academic integrity', a limit set by what each instructor expects. P59 covers instructors' own use of AI for teaching work; consultants recommending tools to students is not that. P04 (instructor sets the rule) is the closer type, with a fit_note.

units.why: Staff 'may recommend AI tools and help students evaluate the results' when allowed; a conditional permission for staff to recommend AI. No type covers staff recommending tools, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: our consultants may recommend AI tools and help students evaluate the results
units.uncovered_note: Writing center consultants may recommend AI tools to students and help them evaluate the results, when the course rules allow.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded UNCOVERED, coder B coded P59. The source says 'When allowable and appropriate, our consultants may recommend AI tools and help students evaluate the results'. This is support staff recommending AI tools to students, not instructor use of AI for teaching work (P59) and not a rule on students' own use. No type states it, so UNCOVERED is kept. Coder B's separate unit 'help students evaluate the results' (P31) is folded in here because it is the same sentence and does not state a student duty to verify.

units.why: States 'Our primary goal is, as always, to help students learn how to grow as writers', the Center's goal that frames its AI support. It is a rationale (informs) that does not say AI shortcuts practice, so P41 would be a stretch.
units.anchor: Our primary goal is, as always, to help students learn how to grow as writers.
units.uncovered_note: The Center's primary goal is to help students learn to grow as writers, which frames its AI support.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this, coding it P41 (AI shortcuts practice). The source says 'Our primary goal is, as always, to help students learn how to grow as writers'. It is a real statement of purpose in the policy, so kept, but it does not say AI undermines practice, so P41 does not fit; coded UNCOVERED rather than stretched.

units.why: Says leveraging AI responsibly can improve 'writing, research, evaluation, and revision skills at different stages of the writing process'; a permission for AI-supported writing, P91 (writing support) rather than P18 because it permits, not separates.
units.anchor: learning to leverage AI responsibly to improve their writing, research, evaluation, and revision skills

units.why: Says 'We continue to focus on writing practices and critical thinking in all our sessions', describing the Center's own practice with no obligation wording, so informs; P32 (students stay the primary thinker) is the closest type.
units.anchor: We continue to focus on writing practices and critical thinking in all our sessions.
units.fit_note: Describes the Center's focus, not a rule on students; the type is about the student staying the primary problem-solver.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on type P32 and actor but A set modality should and B informs. The source says 'We continue to focus on writing practices and critical thinking in all our sessions', a description of the Center's own practice with no 'should' or 'must' wording, so informs.

units.why: 'We encourage writers at all levels to consider the ethical dimensions of AI use' invites ethical reflection, which P53 covers. It is an encouragement, hence 'should'.
units.anchor: We encourage writers at all levels to consider the ethical dimensions of AI use
units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this. The source says 'We encourage writers at all levels to consider the ethical dimensions of AI use', a separate encouragement from the one on attribution and citation. Kept as P53 (ethical concerns).

units.why: Encourages writers to consider ethical dimensions, 'emphasizing original work', i.e. work students submit is their own; P29.
units.anchor: emphasizing original work, attribution and citation when appropriate
units.frag_start: We encourage writers at all levels
units.fit_note: Original work is one of several emphases listed in a single phrase.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this separately; coder B combined original work and attribution into one P24 unit. The source says 'emphasizing original work, attribution and citation when appropriate'. Original work (students own what they submit) and attribution/citation are two distinct rules, so they are kept as two units: P29 here and P24 for the attribution part.

units.why: The same sentence stresses 'attribution and citation when appropriate', a disclosure expectation for AI use; P24 with soft wording (encourage, when appropriate).
units.fit_note: Conditional ('when appropriate'); does not say what the citation must contain.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P24. Coder B anchored the whole phrase and noted P29 for original work; the original-work part is a separate unit here, so this unit is anchored on 'attribution and citation when appropriate' only.

units.why: Names 'AI's limitations, biases, and environmental impacts' as things writers should understand; ethical and environmental concerns, P53.
units.anchor: an understanding of AI's limitations, biases, and environmental impacts
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on type and modality but A set phase general and B during-work. The sentence is in the Center's list of what it emphasizes with writers in sessions ('We encourage writers at all levels to consider the ethical dimensions of AI use, emphasizing ... an understanding of AI's limitations, biases, and environmental impacts'), so it applies while students work with consultants: during-work.

units.why: Says the Center may guide students in 'integrating AI tools in ways that enhance their learning experience while upholding the values and expectations of their instructors', a conditional welcome of AI; P02 fits the permit-with-conditions stance.
units.anchor: guiding students in integrating AI tools in ways that enhance their learning experience
units.frag_start: In some cases, that may mean
units.frag_end: expectations of their instructors and the University of Miami.
units.fit_note: Permission is conditional on instructor expectations and applies to staff guidance, not a general default. Permission is conditional on instructor and university expectations and is framed as staff guidance, not a default rule.

units.why: The note 'This statement was constructed with input from ChatGPT 4o' says how the policy was made, P84.
units.anchor: This statement was constructed with input from ChatGPT 4o
units.fit_note: Disclosure of AI use in drafting the policy statement itself, not in grading, feedback or instruction.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P84, coder B coded P47. The source note 'This statement was constructed with input from ChatGPT 4o' says how the policy itself was made. P47 is about disclosing an instructor's AI use to students (grading, feedback, instruction), which this is not. P84 (how and by whom the policy was made) fits.

notes: Only one included document: a Writing Center unit-level policy, not university-wide; no university, school or computing policy found, course layer deferred. Search snippets attributing a prohibit-unless-permitted policy to Miami came from a third-party aggregator and were not verified.
